\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The measured object}

Consider a family of transformer language models of increasing parameter count,
evaluated at increasing context lengths, and for each (model, context) pair record
the smallest per-query \emph{key budget} at which task quality has not yet
degraded. Plotted against budget, quality falls sharply and then plateaus; the
corner of that curve is the \emph{knee}, and the recorded number is the knee
budget.

Index the context lengths by octaves: column $j\in\N$ corresponds to context length
$512\cdot 2^{j}$. Index the models by a \emph{scale index} $s$. For the family we
study---call it the reference family---the measured table is

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
model & $j=0$ ($512$) & $j=1$ ($1024$) & $j=2$ ($2048$) & $j=3$ ($4096$)\\
\midrule
$0.5$B \ ($s=0$) & $16$ & $20$ & $24$ & $28$\\
$1.5$B \ ($s=1$) & $16$ & $16$ & $20$ & $24$\\
$7$B \ \ \ ($s=2$) & $16$ & $16$ & $16$ & $20$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Each row is the row above it shifted one column to the right, with the vacated
left cells filled by the base value $16$.

\subsection{The discrete octave shift law}

\begin{definition}[Chain]
A \emph{chain} is a function $K:\N\to\N$, interpreted as the knee budget at $j$
octaves of context above the base context of a reference model.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Discrete shift]
For $s\in\N$ the \emph{shift} of a chain is $(\operatorname{shift}K\,s)(j)=K(j\dsub s)$,
with $\dsub$ truncated subtraction on $\N$.
\end{definition}

The discrete theory establishes that a measured scale family---a two-variable
table satisfying the \emph{exchange law} $k(s+a,j+a)=k(s,j)$ and \emph{base-context
inertia} $k(s,0)=k(0,0)$---is exactly $k(s,j)=K(j\dsub s)$ for its base chain
$K=k(0,\cdot)$, and that $\operatorname{shift}$ is an action of $(\N,+)$. For the
reference family the base chain is arithmetic, $K(j)=16+4j$.

\subsection{The problem}

An action of $(\N,+)$ has no element strictly between ``shift by one'' and ``shift
by two''. A $3$B model lies between the $1.5$B and $7$B rows, and the discrete law
is structurally incapable of assigning it a budget. The competing hypothesis is
blunt: \emph{scale acts only discretely, and each model family needs its own
chain}.

This paper tests that hypothesis by formalising the extension as a monotone
interpolation problem, proving existence, delimiting non-uniqueness exactly, and
identifying the additional axiom that restores uniqueness. We then compute the
resulting continuous table, sweep the $3$B cell, and quantify the exact error
incurred by discretising the scale axis.

\section{The scale flow}

\subsection{Ordered subtraction is the hinge}

The informal continuous law one would write down is
$k^*(\sigma,j)=K_0\bigl(\max(j-\sigma,0)\bigr)$. The clamp $\max(\cdot,0)$ looks
like an ad hoc guard. It is not. In any commutative ordered monoid with ordered
subtraction, $x\dsub y$ is characterised by the adjunction
$x\dsub y\le z \iff x\le y+z$. On $\N$ this is truncated subtraction; on $\Rnn$ it
is exactly $\max(x-y,0)$. The two formulas are one formula in two monoids.

\begin{definition}[Real knee profile]
A \emph{real knee profile} is a function $K_0:\Rnn\to\mathbb{R}$. The value
$K_0(x)$ is the key budget at $x$ octaves of context above the model's own base
context. The domain is $\Rnn$ because a model is never queried below its base
context; the chain is clamped there, not extrapolated.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scale flow]
For $\sigma\in\Rnn$ define $\rho_\sigma K_0:\Rnn\to\mathbb{R}$ by
\[
(\rho_\sigma K_0)(t)=K_0(t\dsub\sigma)=K_0\bigl(\max(t-\sigma,0)\bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

\subsection{The flow is a monoid action}

\begin{theorem}[Extension of the shift action]\label{thm:action}
For every real profile $K_0$ and all $a,b\in\Rnn$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\rho_0K_0=K_0$;
\item $\rho_b(\rho_aK_0)=\rho_{a+b}K_0$;
\item \textup{(exchange)} $(\rho_{\sigma+a}K_0)(t+a)=(\rho_\sigma K_0)(t)$ for all
$\sigma,t,a\ge 0$;
\item \textup{(boundary)} if $t\le\sigma$ then $(\rho_\sigma K_0)(t)=K_0(0)$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently $\sigma\mapsto\rho_\sigma$ is an action of the additive monoid
$(\Rnn,+)$ on real knee profiles.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) is $t\dsub 0=t$. (2) is the ordered-subtraction identity
$(t\dsub a)\dsub b=t\dsub(a+b)$, which holds in any such monoid and follows from
the adjunction. (3) is cancellation of a common summand,
$(t+a)\dsub(\sigma+a)=t\dsub\sigma$. (4) is $t\dsub\sigma=0$ for $t\le\sigma$.
\end{proof}

Thus ``the shift action extends from $(\N,+)$ to $(\Rnn,+)$'' is a theorem about a
structure, not a slogan: $\rho$ is a bona fide monoid action, and item (2) is its
associativity law. If $K_0$ is monotone then so is $\rho_\sigma K_0$ for every
$\sigma$, and for fixed $t$ the map $\sigma\mapsto(\rho_\sigma K_0)(t)$ is
antitone.

\subsection{The flow restricts to the measurements}

\begin{lemma}[Cast compatibility]\label{lem:cast}
For $s,j\in\N$, the image of $j\dsub s$ under $\N\hookrightarrow\Rnn$ equals
$(j)\dsub(s)$ computed in $\Rnn$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Two cases. If $j\le s$ both sides are $0$. If $s\le j$ then $(j-s)+s=j$ in $\N$,
hence also in $\Rnn$ after casting, and applying $\dsub s$ recovers the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction]\label{thm:restrict}
Let $K$ be a measured chain and $K_0$ a real profile with $K_0(n)=K(n)$ for all
$n\in\N$. Then $(\rho_sK_0)(j)=K(j\dsub s)=k(s,j)$ for all $s,j\in\N$: the
continuous table reproduces every measured cell.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:cast} and the interpolation hypothesis.
\end{proof}

This is the legitimacy condition for the whole programme: the extension adds
structure between the measured cells and disturbs none of them.

\section{Continuous rigidity}

\begin{definition}[Scale flow table]
A \emph{scale flow} is a function $F:\Rnn\times\Rnn\to\mathbb{R}$ such that
$F(0,\cdot)$ is monotone (\emph{base monotonicity}); $F(\sigma+a,t+a)=F(\sigma,t)$
for all $\sigma,t,a\ge0$ (\emph{exchange}); and $F(\sigma,0)=F(0,0)$ for all
$\sigma$ (\emph{base-context inertia}).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Continuous rigidity]\label{thm:rigid}
Every scale flow satisfies
\[
F(\sigma,t)=F\bigl(0,\;t\dsub\sigma\bigr)=\bigl(\rho_\sigma F(0,\cdot)\bigr)(t).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Fix $\sigma,t$. If $t\le\sigma$, apply exchange to the base pair $(\sigma-t,0)$
with increment $a=t$: since $(\sigma-t)+t=\sigma$ and $0+t=t$ we get
$F(\sigma,t)=F(\sigma-t,0)$, which base-context inertia flattens to $F(0,0)$;
and $t\dsub\sigma=0$. If $\sigma\le t$, apply exchange to the base pair
$(0,t-\sigma)$ with increment $a=\sigma$: $F(\sigma,t)=F(0,t-\sigma)=F(0,t\dsub\sigma)$.
\end{proof}

The discrete analogue proves the same statement by induction on the number of
scale steps; the real-parameter version needs none, because a single translation
reaches any cell. Continuity of the parameter \emph{simplifies} the argument.

\begin{corollary}[Structural refutations]\label{cor:refut}
Let $F$ be a scale flow.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textup{(No amplification of sensitivity.)} For each fixed $t$, the map
$\sigma\mapsto F(\sigma,t)$ is antitone: a larger model never requires a larger
budget at the same context.
\item \textup{(No flattening.)} If $F(0,\cdot)$ is unbounded above, so is
$F(\sigma,\cdot)$ for every $\sigma$.
\item Every $F(\sigma,\cdot)$ is monotone.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) By Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}, $F(\sigma,t)=F(0,t\dsub\sigma)$ and
$\sigma\mapsto t\dsub\sigma$ is antitone; compose with base monotonicity.
(2) Given $b$, pick $t$ with $F(0,t)>b$; then
$F(\sigma,t+\sigma)=F(0,(t+\sigma)\dsub\sigma)=F(0,t)>b$.
(3) Compose base monotonicity with monotonicity of $t\mapsto t\dsub\sigma$.
\end{proof}

These refute, structurally rather than empirically, the folklore claims that scale
amplifies context sensitivity and that scale flattens the context axis. Scaling
\emph{translates} the difficulty curve.

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz transport]\label{thm:lip}
Let $F$ be a scale flow whose base profile has slope at most $\delta\ge0$, i.e.
$F(0,y)-F(0,x)\le\delta(y-x)$ whenever $x\le y$. Then
\[
\bigl|F(\sigma,t)-F(\sigma+h,t)\bigr|\le\delta h
\qquad\text{for all }\sigma,t,h\ge0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:refut}(1) the difference is nonnegative, so the absolute
value may be dropped. By Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid} it equals
$F(0,t\dsub\sigma)-F(0,t\dsub(\sigma+h))$ with
$t\dsub(\sigma+h)\le t\dsub\sigma$, so the slope bound applies with gap
$(t\dsub\sigma)-(t\dsub(\sigma+h))$. The last step is the ordered-subtraction
inequality $(t\dsub\sigma)-(t\dsub(\sigma+h))\le h$, which follows from
$t\le (t\dsub(\sigma+h))+\sigma+h$.
\end{proof}

Deployment tables built from the flow are therefore Lipschitz in scale:
interpolating the model-size axis introduces no cliffs between measured rows.

\begin{theorem}[Real-rate identifiability]\label{thm:inj}
If $K_0$ is strictly monotone and $\rho_aK_0=\rho_bK_0$, then $a=b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Suppose $a<b$ and evaluate both sides at $t=b$: the right side is $K_0(0)$, the
left is $K_0(b-a)$ with $b-a>0$, contradicting strict monotonicity. Symmetrically
for $b<a$.
\end{proof}

Passing from $(\N,+)$ to $(\Rnn,+)$ therefore introduces no gauge freedom in the
scale parameter.

\section{The interpolation problem}

\subsection{Existence: the ramp basis}

\begin{definition}[Unit ramp]
$r(x)=\min\bigl(1,\max(x,0)\bigr)$: zero below $0$, linear on $[0,1]$, one above
$1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Ramp-basis interpolant]
For a chain $K$ with octave increments $d_i=K(i+1)-K(i)$, set
\[
\PL_K(t)=K(0)+\sum_{i<\lceil t\rceil} d_i\, r(t-i).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:pl}
If $K$ is monotone then $\PL_K$ is monotone, and $\PL_K(n)=K(n)$ for all $n\in\N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\emph{Monotonicity.} Let $t\le u$, so $\lceil t\rceil\le\lceil u\rceil$. Over the
common index range $i<\lceil t\rceil$ each summand increases, because $r$ is
monotone and each coefficient $d_i\ge0$; the extra indices
$\lceil t\rceil\le i<\lceil u\rceil$ contribute terms $d_i r(u-i)\ge0$.
Monotonicity is thus structural---nonnegative coefficients on monotone basis
functions---rather than a case analysis on floors.
\emph{Interpolation.} At $t=n$ every index $i<n$ has $n-i\ge1$, so $r(n-i)=1$ and
the sum telescopes to $K(0)+\sum_{i<n}(K(i+1)-K(i))=K(n)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Interpolation criterion]\label{thm:criterion}
For a chain $K$ the following are equivalent: \textup{(1)} there exists a monotone
real profile $K_0$ with $K_0(n)=K(n)$ for all $n$; \textup{(2)} $K$ is monotone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(2)$\Rightarrow$(1) is Theorem~\ref{thm:pl}. (1)$\Rightarrow$(2): for $a\le b$ in
$\N$, $K(a)=K_0(a)\le K_0(b)=K(b)$.
\end{proof}

Combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:action}: \emph{the real-parameter extension is
available exactly on the tables the discrete theory already admits.} No measured
table is lost, and a non-monotone table can never be interpolated.

\begin{corollary}[Extension for every measured family]
For any scale family $F$ obeying the discrete exchange and boundary laws there is
a monotone real profile $K_0$ with $K_0\bigl((j)\dsub(s)\bigr)=F(s,j)$ for all
$s,j\in\N$: the action extends from $(\N,+)$ to $(\Rnn,+)$ without losing a cell.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $K_0=\PL_{F(0,\cdot)}$ and combine Theorem~\ref{thm:pl},
Lemma~\ref{lem:cast}, and the discrete rigidity $F(s,j)=F(0,j\dsub s)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Uniqueness fails}

\begin{definition}[Staircase interpolant]
$\ST_K(t)=K(\lceil t\rceil)$: round the context up to the next measured octave.
\end{definition}

$\ST_K$ is monotone whenever $K$ is, and $\ST_K(n)=K(n)$.

\begin{theorem}[Non-uniqueness]\label{thm:nonuniq}
For the reference base chain $K(j)=16+4j$, both $\PL_K$ and $\ST_K$ are monotone
and interpolate every measured cell, yet at the half-octave
\[
\PL_K(1/2)=18,\qquad \ST_K(1/2)=20 .
\]
They disagree by four keys.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\lceil 1/2\rceil=1$, so $\PL_K(1/2)=K(0)+d_0\,r(1/2)=16+4\cdot\tfrac12=18$, while
$\ST_K(1/2)=K(1)=20$.
\end{proof}

Monotone interpolation alone therefore does not determine intermediate model
sizes. This refutes the natural conjecture and forces the search for an additional
axiom.

\subsection{The repair: stationary increments}

The tempting repair---impose smoothness---is unmotivated: smoothness is an
analytic convenience with no operational content. The correct condition is a
\emph{flow} condition.

\begin{definition}[Stationary increments]
A profile $K_0$ has \emph{stationary increments} if
\[
K_0(t+u)-K_0(t)=K_0(u)-K_0(0)\qquad\text{for all }t,u\in\Rnn,
\]
i.e. the change over an interval depends only on its length. This is the defining
homogeneity property of a one-parameter flow.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy rigidity on $\Rnn$]\label{lem:cauchy}
If $g:\Rnn\to\mathbb{R}$ is monotone and additive, $g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$, then
$g(t)=g(1)\,t$ for all $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Additivity gives $g(0)=0$ and, by induction, $g(nx)=n\,g(x)$ for $n\in\N$;
monotonicity gives $g(1)\ge0$. Fix $t$ and $n\ge1$ and put $m=\lfloor nt\rfloor$,
so $m\le nt\le m+1$. Applying the monotone $g$ and using $g(m)=m\,g(1)$,
$g(m+1)=(m+1)g(1)$, $g(nt)=n\,g(t)$ gives
\[
m\,g(1)\;\le\;n\,g(t)\;\le\;(m+1)\,g(1).
\]
Multiplying $m\le nt\le m+1$ by $g(1)\ge0$ bounds $n\,t\,g(1)$ by the same two
quantities. Subtracting, $|n\,g(t)-n\,t\,g(1)|\le g(1)$, hence
$|g(t)-g(1)t|\le g(1)/n$ for every $n\ge1$, and letting $n\to\infty$ gives the
claim.
\end{proof}

No continuity, measurability or rationality hypothesis is used: monotonicity does
the work that regularity assumptions usually do. This is why the resulting theorem
is a structural statement about flows rather than a smoothness assumption in
disguise.

\begin{theorem}[Generator theorem]\label{thm:gen}
A monotone real profile with stationary increments is affine:
\[
K_0(t)=K_0(0)+\delta\,t,\qquad \delta:=K_0(1)-K_0(0).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Put $g(t)=K_0(t)-K_0(0)$. Monotonicity of $K_0$ gives monotonicity of $g$;
stationarity is exactly additivity of $g$. Lemma~\ref{lem:cauchy} gives
$g(t)=g(1)t$.
\end{proof}

Combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:nonuniq} this pins the boundary exactly:
\emph{monotonicity alone leaves a family of interpolants; monotonicity plus
stationary increments leaves precisely one.} The constant $\delta$ is the
\emph{keys-per-octave rate}.

\subsection{Arithmetic chains and the canonical table}

\begin{definition}[Affine profile]
$A_{k_0,\delta}(t)=k_0+\delta t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Existence and uniqueness for arithmetic chains]\label{thm:arith}
Let $K$ be a chain with $K(j)=k_0+\delta j$ for all $j$, with $\delta\ge0$. Then
$A_{k_0,\delta}$ is monotone, interpolates $K$, and has stationary increments;
and it is the \emph{only} monotone interpolant of $K$ with stationary increments.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The first part is direct computation. For uniqueness, let $K_0$ be another such
interpolant; evaluation at $0$ and $1$ gives $K_0(0)=k_0$ and $K_0(1)=k_0+\delta$,
and Theorem~\ref{thm:gen} then gives $K_0(t)=k_0+\delta t$.
\end{proof}

For the reference family $k_0=16$ and $\delta=4$. Applying
Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}:

\begin{corollary}[The canonical real table]\label{cor:canon}
\[
k^*(\sigma,t)=k_0+\delta\,(t-\sigma)^{+}=16+4\max(t-\sigma,0).
\]
\end{corollary}

For $\delta\ge0$ the table is antitone in $\sigma$ and monotone in $t$. Hence the
\emph{sweep bracket}: if $\sigma_1\le\sigma\le\sigma_2$ then
$k^*(\sigma_2,t)\le k^*(\sigma,t)\le k^*(\sigma_1,t)$ for every $t$---an
unmeasured model between two measured ones has its whole knee chain bracketed by
theirs.

\begin{theorem}[Restriction to the measured cells]
For all $s,j\in\N$, $k^*(s,j)=k(s,j)$. In particular
$k^*(0,\cdot)=(16,20,24,28,\dots)$, $k^*(1,\cdot)=(16,16,20,24,\dots)$ and
$k^*(2,\cdot)=(16,16,16,20,\dots)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\max(j-s,0)=j\dsub s$ for naturals cast to $\mathbb{R}$, and
$K(j\dsub s)=16+4(j\dsub s)$.
\end{proof}

\section{The generator and the transport equation}

\begin{theorem}[Generator]\label{thm:generator}
For $\sigma<t$,
\[
\frac{\partial k^*}{\partial\sigma}(\sigma,t)=-\delta,
\qquad
\frac{\partial k^*}{\partial t}(\sigma,t)=+\delta .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
On the open region $\{\sigma<t\}$ we have $k^*(\sigma,t)=k_0+\delta(t-\sigma)$;
the table agrees with this affine expression on a neighbourhood of any such point,
and the derivative transports along that local agreement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Transport equation]\label{thm:transport}
For $\sigma<t$,
\[
\frac{\partial k^*}{\partial\sigma}+\frac{\partial k^*}{\partial t}=0 .
\]
\end{theorem}

The table is constant along the direction $(1,1)$ in the (scale, context) plane.
This is the infinitesimal form of the exchange law: one octave of scale is
exchanged for exactly one octave of context, and the exchange rate---the
generator---is the keys-per-octave rate $\delta$. Equivalently, scale and context
enter the table only through the combination $t-\sigma$, i.e. through the ratio
$\mathrm{ctx}/2^{\sigma}$, now for real $\sigma$.

\section{Calibrating the scale axis and the 3B sweep}

\subsection{Log-linear calibration}

Parameter counts multiply, so the natural calibration of the scale axis is
logarithmic, anchored on the two consecutive measured rows $1.5$B $\mapsto 1$ and
$7$B $\mapsto 2$.

\begin{definition}[Scale index]
For $N>0$ (model size in billions of parameters),
\[
\si(N)=1+\frac{\log(N/1.5)}{\log(14/3)} .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}
$\si(1.5)=1$, $\si(7)=2$, and $\si$ is strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\log 1=0$; $7/1.5=14/3$; strict monotonicity follows from that of $\log$ and
positivity of $\log(14/3)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The 3B scale index]\label{thm:si3}
$\dfrac{7}{5}<\si(3)<\dfrac{3}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Since $3/1.5=2$, $\si(3)=1+\varrho$ with $\varrho=\log 2/\log(14/3)$; it suffices
to bound $\varrho$ strictly between $2/5$ and $1/2$. As $\log(14/3)>0$, the bound
$\varrho<1/2$ is equivalent to $2\log 2<\log(14/3)$, i.e. $4<14/3$; the bound
$2/5<\varrho$ is equivalent to $2\log(14/3)<5\log2$, i.e. $(14/3)^2<2^5$, i.e.
$196/9<32$. Both hold.
\end{proof}

Numerically $\si(3)=1.44997\ldots$: the $3$B model sits just short of half an
octave past the $1.5$B row. In particular $1<\si(3)<2$ and $\si(3)\ne s$ for every
$s\in\N$: \emph{the offset is strictly fractional.}

\subsection{The predicted 3B chain}

Write $k_{3\mathrm{B}}(t)=k^*(\si(3),t)$.

\begin{theorem}[Flat region]
$k_{3\mathrm{B}}(0)=k_{3\mathrm{B}}(1)=16$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Both $0$ and $1$ are below $\si(3)>7/5>1$, so the clamp is active.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[3B at $2048$ tokens]\label{thm:3B2048}
\[
k^*(2,2)<k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)<k^*(1,2),\qquad
18<k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)<\tfrac{92}{5}=18.4,\qquad
\lceil k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)\rceil=19 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Since $\si(3)<3/2<2$ the clamp is inactive:
$k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)=16+4(2-\si(3))$. Theorem~\ref{thm:si3} gives
$2-\si(3)\in(1/2,3/5)$, so the value lies in $(18,18.4)$. The measured neighbours
are $k^*(2,2)=16$ and $k^*(1,2)=20$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[3B at $4096$ tokens]
\[
k^*(2,3)<k_{3\mathrm{B}}(3)<k^*(1,3),\qquad
22<k_{3\mathrm{B}}(3)<\tfrac{112}{5}=22.4,\qquad
\lceil k_{3\mathrm{B}}(3)\rceil=23,
\]
with measured neighbours $k^*(2,3)=20$ and $k^*(1,3)=24$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotone in model size]
For every $t$, $k^*(\si(7),t)\le k_{3\mathrm{B}}(t)\le k^*(\si(1.5),t)$: the
interpolated deployment table never crosses a measured one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
model & $512$ & $1024$ & $2048$ & $4096$\\
\midrule
$1.5$B \ ($\sigma=1$) & $16$ & $16$ & $20$ & $24$\\
$\mathbf{3}$\textbf{B} \ ($\sigma\approx1.44997$) & $\mathbf{16}$ & $\mathbf{16}$ &
$\mathbf{19}$ (from $18.20$) & $\mathbf{23}$ (from $22.20$)\\
$7$B \ \ \ ($\sigma=2$) & $16$ & $16$ & $16$ & $20$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{Falsifiability}

\begin{theorem}[The prediction is not a discrete cell]
For every $s\in\N$, $k^*(s,2)\ne k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $s\ge2$ the clamp gives $k^*(s,2)=16<18<k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)$. If $s\le1$ then
$k^*(s,2)=16+4(2-s)\ge20>18.4>k_{3\mathrm{B}}(2)$.
\end{proof}

A purely discrete action can only predict integer translates: at $2048$ tokens it
must say $16$ or $20$. The flow says $19$. A measured $3$B knee of $16$ or $20$
refutes the extension; a measured $19$ confirms it.

\section{What a family owns: identifiability and offset conjugacy}

\begin{theorem}[Rate identifiability]\label{thm:ident}
Let $\delta'>0$ and suppose
\[
k_0+\delta(t-a)^{+}=k_0'+\delta'(t-b)^{+}\qquad\text{for all }t\in\mathbb{R}.
\]
Then $k_0=k_0'$, $\delta=\delta'$ and $a=b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Evaluate at $t=\min(a,b)$: both clamps are inactive, so $k_0=k_0'$. Let
$M=\max(a,b)$ and evaluate at $t=M$ and $t=M+1$, where both clamps are active;
subtracting the two identities yields $\delta=\delta'$, and substituting back and
cancelling the nonzero $\delta'$ yields $a=b$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Forced parameters]
Any clamped-affine family at scale offset $0$ reproducing the measured cells
$k^*(0,0)=16$ and $k^*(0,1)=20$ has $k_0=16$ and $\delta=4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Offset conjugacy]
Writing $k^*_a(t)=k_0+\delta(t-a)^{+}$, two clamped-affine tables with the same
$(k_0,\delta)$ are translates along the flow direction $(1,1)$:
$k^*_{a+h}(t+h)=k^*_a(t)$ for all $t,h$.
\end{theorem}

Together these settle the competing hypothesis precisely. The chain and the rate
are \emph{shared} across the family; the only freedom a model owns, once the
profile is fixed, is a single number---its offset on the scale axis---and that
offset may be genuinely fractional. So ``each family needs its own chain'' is too
coarse in one direction, and the ``one universal table'' reading is too strong in
the other.

\section{The budget adjunction and the exact discretisation defect}

\subsection{Reading the table backwards}

\begin{definition}[Reach]
For a profile with base knee $k_0$ and rate $\delta>0$, the \emph{reach} of a
budget $b\ge k_0$ is $R(b)=(b-k_0)/\delta\ \ge 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Budget adjunction]\label{thm:adj}
For $\delta>0$ and $b\ge k_0$, and for all real $\sigma,t$,
\[
k^*(\sigma,t)\le b \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t\le\sigma+R(b).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If $t\le\sigma$ the left side reads $k_0\le b$, true, and the right side holds
since $R\ge0$. If $t\ge\sigma$ the left side reads $k_0+\delta(t-\sigma)\le b$,
which after dividing by $\delta>0$ is $t-\sigma\le(b-k_0)/\delta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Served ray]
The served set at scale $\sigma$ is exactly the closed ray
$\{t: t\le\sigma+R(b)\}$, and its supremum $\sigma+R(b)$ is attained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Continuous budget law]
For every real increment $h$,
\[
\sup\{t: k^*(\sigma+h,t)\le b\}=\bigl(\sigma+R(b)\bigr)+h .
\]
The served boundary is the line $t=\sigma+R(b)$ of slope exactly $1$: a fixed
budget buys one context octave per octave of scale, for real scale. The discrete
law is the restriction of this line to the integer lattice.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The measured instance}

For the reference family with $b=16=k_0$ the reach is $R(16)=0$, so the served
boundary is the diagonal $t=\sigma$: a $16$-key budget buys exactly a model's own
base context. On the integer lattice this says the first \emph{failing} context
octave at scale $s$ is $s+1$---precisely what was measured at $s=0$ and $s=1$ and
predicted at $s=2$.

\subsection{The staircase--triangle defect}

Fix $b=16$ and a scale window $S\in\N$ inside a context window $J\ge S$ wide enough
that no cell is cut off. At integer scale $s$ the served context octaves are
$j=0,\dots,s$, so $s+1$ cells, giving
\[
\#\{\text{served cells}\}=\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}(s+1)=\frac{S(S+1)}{2},
\]
a staircase; while the area under the served boundary $t=\sigma$ over $[0,S]$ is
$\int_0^S\sigma\,d\sigma=S^2/2$, a triangle.

\begin{theorem}[Exact discretisation defect]\label{thm:defect}
For every $S\in\N$ and every $J\ge S$,
\[
\#\{\text{served cells over }[0,S)\}=\int_0^S\sigma\,d\sigma+\frac{S}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$S(S+1)/2-S^2/2=S/2$. The only care needed is the degenerate case $S=0$, where
both sides vanish.
\end{proof}

This is the Euler--Maclaurin half-cell correction, in closed form and with no
error term: the staircase exceeds the triangle by exactly half a cell per scale
row. It is \emph{linear} where the two quantities themselves are quadratic, so it
vanishes to first order---which is the precise sense in which the continuous table
is a faithful interpolation of the measured one rather than a story imposed upon
it.

\section{The tropical reading}

\begin{theorem}[Tropical binomial form]\label{thm:tropform}
For $\delta\ge0$,
\[
k^*(\sigma,t)=\max\bigl(k_0,\;k_0+\delta t-\delta\sigma\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

In the max-plus semiring---tropical addition $\max$, tropical multiplication
ordinary $+$---this exhibits the knee table as a \emph{tropical binomial} in the
two real coordinates: the tropical sum of the constant monomial $k_0$ and the
monomial $k_0+\delta t-\delta\sigma$. Every structural feature of the table now
follows from standard facts about tropical polynomials.

\begin{theorem}[Convexity / diminishing returns]
For $\delta\ge0$, $t\mapsto k^*(\sigma,t)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$, and
$\sigma\mapsto k^*(\sigma,t)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A pointwise maximum of a constant and an affine function is convex: for a convex
combination, each branch is bounded by the corresponding combination of maxima.
Apply with slope $\delta$ in $t$ and slope $-\delta$ in $\sigma$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Corner locus]\label{thm:corner}
Let $\delta>0$ and fix $\sigma$. Then $t\mapsto k^*(\sigma,t)$ is differentiable at
every $t\ne\sigma$ and not differentiable at $t=\sigma$; that is,
\[
\{t: k^*(\sigma,\cdot)\text{ is not differentiable at }t\}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $t<\sigma$ the function is locally constant; for $t>\sigma$ locally affine of
slope $\delta$; both regions are open. At $t=\sigma$ the one-sided derivatives are
$\delta$ from the right and $0$ from the left. A two-sided derivative $d$ would
have to agree with each one-sided derivative on a set with the unique
differentiability property, forcing $d=\delta$ and $d=0$, contradicting
$\delta>0$.
\end{proof}

Deployment-wise: \emph{each model has exactly one knee in its knee table, located
at its own base context.}

\begin{theorem}[Flow invariance of the corner locus]
For $\delta>0$ and all $\sigma,t,a$, the map $k^*(\sigma,\cdot)$ is non-smooth at
$t$ if and only if $k^*(\sigma+a,\cdot)$ is non-smooth at $t+a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:corner} the two conditions are $t=\sigma$ and
$t+a=\sigma+a$, which are the same.
\end{proof}

The corner locus is the diagonal of the (scale, context) plane, hence invariant
under the flow direction $(1,1)$. \emph{The exchange law is precisely the statement
that the tropical hypersurface of the knee table is a line of slope one}, and the
discrete octave shift law is that line sampled at lattice points.

\begin{theorem}[The flow preserves diminishing returns]
If a base profile $K_0:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is convex and monotone, then
$t\mapsto K_0\bigl(\max(t-\sigma,0)\bigr)$ is convex for every $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The clamp is convex with image $[0,\infty)$; a monotone convex function composed
with a convex function is convex, using monotonicity of $K_0$ on the image.
\end{proof}

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{Algorithm A (Chain fitting).}
Given a measured table, extract the base chain $K=k(0,\cdot)$, verify
$k(s,j)=K(j\dsub s)$ on every measured cell, test $K$ for monotonicity
(Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion}), and test $K$ for constant increments. If increments
are constant, output $(k_0,\delta)=(K(0),K(1)-K(0))$ and the closed-form table
$k^*=k_0+\delta(t-\sigma)^{+}$; otherwise fall back to the ramp interpolant of
Theorem~\ref{thm:pl}. Cost: $O(SJ)$ validation, $O(J)$ fitting.

\paragraph{Algorithm B (Interpolated budget).}
Given a target model size $N$, a context length $L$, fitted $(k_0,\delta)$ and
anchors $(N_1,\sigma_1)$, $(N_2,\sigma_2)$: compute $\sigma=\si(N)$ by log-linear
calibration, compute $t=\log_2(L/L_{\text{base}})$, evaluate
$k^*(\sigma,t)=k_0+\delta\max(t-\sigma,0)$, and return $\lceil k^*\rceil$.
Cost $O(1)$; correctness of the bracketing is the sweep bracket, and Lipschitz
stability in $N$ is Theorem~\ref{thm:lip}.

\paragraph{Algorithm C (Reach and served region).}
Given a budget $b$, compute $R=(b-k_0)/\delta$; report the served boundary
$t=\sigma+R$, the discrete served-cell count
$\sum_{s<S}\min(J,\lfloor s+R\rfloor+1)$, the continuous area, and their
difference---which equals $S/2$ exactly in the aligned case $b=k_0$, $J\ge S$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:defect}). Cost $O(S)$.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{What the continuous extension buys}

\emph{Operationally}, it fills in rows: a deployment table becomes a function of a
real model size, Lipschitz in that size, with a closed-form budget and a
falsifiable prediction for any unmeasured model.

\emph{Structurally}, it clarifies what the octave shift law is. In discrete form it
looks like a numerical coincidence about a grid. In continuous form it is a
transport equation whose generator is the keys-per-octave rate; the shift is the
exponential of that generator. The rigidity proof gets \emph{shorter} in the
continuous setting, because a translation replaces an induction.

\emph{Geometrically}, it identifies the table as a tropical binomial with a single
corner on the diagonal, subsuming convexity, the one-knee-per-model fact, and the
exchange law itself into one statement about a tropical hypersurface being a line
of slope one.

\subsection{What was refuted}

\emph{``Monotonicity alone determines intermediate model sizes''}---false, with the
explicit four-key gap of Theorem~\ref{thm:nonuniq}. The correction required
identifying the right axiom, and the right axiom turned out to be a flow axiom
(stationary increments) and not a smoothness axiom;
Lemma~\ref{lem:cauchy}'s freedom from regularity hypotheses is what makes this a
principled rather than a convenient choice.

\emph{``The rate is a gauge artefact of the scale calibration''}---false, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:ident}.

\emph{``Each model family needs its own chain''}---partly false. The chain and rate
are shared; the offset is private, and may be fractional. A purely discrete reading
cannot express a fractional offset and is therefore too coarse.

\subsection{Limitations}

The measured base chain is exactly arithmetic, which is what makes the canonical
table a \emph{binomial} with a single corner. A family with several plateaux would
have a piecewise arithmetic base chain and a table that is a tropical polynomial
with several monomials, whose corner locus is a tropical curve rather than a single
diagonal; the generator theorem then applies only piecewise.

The log-linear calibration of the scale index is an assumption on the
\emph{parametrisation} of the scale axis, not a theorem: it is fixed by two
anchors, and a family with three or more measured rows over-determines it. Our
family does have a third row, and the over-determination is visible. The measured
ladder is not geometric---$1.5/0.5=3$ while $7/1.5=14/3$---so anchoring on the
upper consecutive pair places the $0.5$B model at
$\si(0.5)=1+\log(1/3)/\log(14/3)=0.2868\ldots$ rather than at $0$, and the
interpolated $0.5$B row $(16,19,23,27)$ undershoots the measured $(16,20,24,28)$
by one key.

The knee table itself is exact at every \emph{integer} scale index: the
discrepancy lives entirely in the map from parameter count to scale index, not in
the flow. It says that the scale axis of this family is slightly compressed at the
small end relative to a pure log-linear law---exactly the kind of deviation
Theorem~\ref{thm:ident} forbids from being absorbed into the rate, and hence
exactly the kind a third anchor makes testable. An alternative calibration
anchored on $0.5$B $\mapsto 0$ and $7$B $\mapsto 2$ gives
$\si(3)=2\log 6/\log 14=1.3579\ldots$ and a $2048$-token knee of $18.57$, still
strictly between the measured neighbours and still rounding to a deployable $19$
keys: the headline prediction is robust to the choice of anchor pair, even though
the exact value is not.

Finally, the defect $S/2$ is exact for the aligned budget $b=k_0$ and a wide-enough
context window; for general budgets the same computation acquires a bounded
fractional-part contribution.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Tropical hypersurface rigidity for multi-knee profiles]
Any finite max-plus profile in the $(\sigma,t)$ plane whose corner locus is
invariant under the direction $(1,1)$ is a tropical polynomial in the single
variable $t-\sigma$.
\end{conjecture}

A measured profile with several plateaux is a tropical polynomial with several
monomials, whose corner locus is a tropical curve rather than a single diagonal.
The flow-invariance argument used nothing about the \emph{number} of monomials: the
exchange law says only that the corner locus is invariant under $(1,1)$. The
one-corner case (Theorem~\ref{thm:corner}) is settled, so an induction on the
number of corners has a base.

\emph{Non-arithmetic chains.} For a chain that is monotone but not arithmetic,
existence and non-uniqueness hold, but stationary increments fail globally. The
right statement is presumably a piecewise generator theorem, with the profile
affine on each plateau and the corner locus a polyhedral curve.

\emph{Over-determined calibration.} With three or more measured rows the log-linear
scale index becomes testable. Deviations would be informative: a systematically
compressed axis at large $N$ would show up as curvature in $\si$, which the
identifiability theorem forbids from being absorbed into the rate.

\emph{Second-order discretisation.} The defect $S/2$ is the first Euler--Maclaurin
term. For general budgets one expects a bounded oscillatory correction governed by
the fractional part of $\sigma+R$; a clean closed form would give error bars on
interpolated tables at arbitrary budgets.

\emph{Empirical falsification.} The sharpest immediate step is to measure a $3$B
model at $2048$ tokens. The flow predicts a knee in $(18,18.4)$ and a deployable
budget of $19$ keys; a measured $16$ or $20$ refutes the real-parameter extension
outright.

\section{Conclusion}

The awkward clamp in the discrete octave shift law---the truncated subtraction that
makes $j-s$ vanish when $s$ exceeds $j$---was never a bookkeeping wart. It is
ordered subtraction, an operation that exists just as naturally in $\Rnn$ as in
$\N$, and reading it there lifts the entire discrete theory verbatim to a
one-parameter flow.

The lift is legitimate (it restricts to every measured cell), rigid (two local laws
determine the whole plane), conditionally unique (monotonicity is not enough;
monotonicity plus stationary increments is exactly enough), generated by an
identifiable rate satisfying a transport equation, geometrically transparent (a
tropical binomial with a single corner on the diagonal), and quantitatively honest
about its own discretisation error (exactly $S/2$, in closed form).

Its practical output is a row that nobody measured: a three-billion-parameter model
at $2048$ tokens of context wants $19$ keys---a number no integer scale index can
produce, and one that a single afternoon of measurement can confirm or destroy.

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

# Measured data (the reference family)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

BASE_CTX: int = 512                 # context length of octave 0
K0_BASE: float = 16.0               # base knee, in keys
DELTA: float = 4.0                  # keys per octave

# 1. Ordered subtraction, in both monoids
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def nat_tsub(j: int, s: int) -> int:
    """Truncated subtraction in (N, +): j - s clamped at 0."""
    return j - s if j >= s else 0


def real_tsub(t: float, s: float) -> float:
    """Ordered subtraction in (R>=0, +): exactly the clamp max(t - s, 0)."""
    return max(t - s, 0.0)


def base_chain(j: int) -> int:

    return 16 + 4 * j


def shift(chain: Callable[[int], int], s: int) -> Callable[[int], int]:
    """The discrete octave shift: (shift K s)(j) = K(j - s), truncated."""
    return lambda j: chain(nat_tsub(j, s))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The canonical real table
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kstar(k0: float, delta: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
    """k*(sigma, t) = k0 + delta * (t - sigma)^+  — the canonical real table."""
    return k0 + delta * real_tsub(t, sigma)


def kstar_tropical(k0: float, delta: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
    """Tropical binomial form: max-plus sum of monomials k0 and k0 + d t - d s."""
    return max(k0, k0 + delta * t - delta * sigma)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Interpolants of a measured chain
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ramp(x: float) -> float:
    """Unit ramp: 0 below 0, linear on [0, 1], 1 above 1."""
    return min(1.0, max(x, 0.0))


def pl_interp(chain: Callable[[int], int], t: float) -> float:
    """Ramp-basis (piecewise-linear) interpolant of a measured chain.

    PL_K(t) = K(0) + sum_{i < ceil(t)} (K(i+1) - K(i)) * ramp(t - i).
    Monotone whenever K is, because every coefficient is nonnegative and every
    basis function is monotone.
    """
    total = float(chain(0))
    for i in range(math.ceil(t)):
        total += (chain(i + 1) - chain(i)) * ramp(t - i)
    return total


def ceil_interp(chain: Callable[[int], int], t: float) -> float:
    """Staircase interpolant: round the context octave up to the next measured one."""
    return float(chain(math.ceil(t)))


def affine_interp(k0: float, delta: float, t: float) -> float:
    """The affine profile k0 + delta * t (unique monotone stationary interpolant)."""
    return k0 + delta * t


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Scale-axis calibration
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def scale_index(n_billion: float) -> float:
    """Log-linear scale index, anchored at 1.5B -> 1 and 7B -> 2."""
    return 1.0 + math.log(n_billion / 1.5) / math.log(14.0 / 3.0)


def deployable_budget(n_billion: float, ctx_tokens: int,
                      k0: float = K0_BASE, delta: float = DELTA) -> int:
    """Interpolated, deployable (integer) key budget for any model size / context."""
    sigma = scale_index(n_billion)
    t = math.log2(ctx_tokens / BASE_CTX)
    return math.ceil(kstar(k0, delta, sigma, t))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Budget reach and served region
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def reach(k0: float, delta: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Reach of a budget: the number of context octaves above base it buys."""
    return (b - k0) / delta


def served_cells(k0: float, delta: float, b: float, S: int, J: int) -> int:
    """Number of served cells of the DISCRETE table over scale rows 0..S-1."""
    count = 0
    for s in range(S):
        for j in range(J + 1):
            if kstar(k0, delta, float(s), float(j)) <= b + 1e-12:
                count += 1
    return count


def served_area(k0: float, delta: float, b: float, S: float) -> float:
    """Area under the CONTINUOUS served boundary t = sigma + reach over [0, S]."""
    r = reach(k0, delta, b)
    # integral_0^S (sigma + r) dsigma  =  S^2/2 + r*S ; with r = 0 this is S^2/2.
    return S * S / 2.0 + r * S

def demo_octave_shift_law() -> bool:
    header("1. The discrete octave shift law: one chain, translated")
    print("  Measured table (rows = scale index, cols = context octave 0..3):")
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        print(f"    sigma = {s} : {row}")
    print()
    print("  Claim: every cell equals K(j - s) with K(j) = 16 + 4j, truncated.")
    ok = True
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        shifted = [shift(base_chain, s)(j) for j in range(len(row))]
        ok &= check(f"row sigma = {s} is the base chain shifted by {s}",
                    shifted == row, f"{shifted}")
    return ok


def demo_monoid_action() -> bool:
    header("2. The shift extends to an action of (R>=0, +)")
    print("  rho_s K(t) = K(max(t - s, 0)).  Check rho_0 = id and")
    print("  rho_b o rho_a = rho_{a+b} at many random-ish sample points.")
    profile = lambda x: affine_interp(K0_BASE, DELTA, x)
    ok = True
    samples = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.3333, 2.0, 2.7, 3.5, 5.0]
    ok &= check("rho_0 is the identity",
                all(abs(profile(real_tsub(t, 0.0)) - profile(t)) < 1e-12
                    for t in samples))
    pairs = [(0.3, 0.7), (1.0, 1.0), (0.45, 2.2), (1.44997, 0.55003)]
    good = True
    for a, b in pairs:
        for t in samples:
            lhs = profile(real_tsub(real_tsub(t, a), b))
            rhs = profile(real_tsub(t, a + b))
            good &= abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-12
    ok &= check("rho_b o rho_a = rho_{a+b} (associativity of the action)", good)

    # exchange law
    good = all(
        abs(profile(real_tsub(t + a, s + a)) - profile(real_tsub(t, s))) < 1e-12
        for s in samples for t in samples for a in (0.0, 0.5, 1.7)
    )
    ok &= check("exchange law: a octaves of scale buy a octaves of context", good)
    return ok


def demo_restriction() -> bool:
    header("3. The real flow restricts to the measured cells")
    ok = True
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        vals = [kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, float(s), float(j)) for j in range(len(row))]
        ok &= check(f"k*({s}, j) reproduces the sigma = {s} row",
                    all(abs(v - m) < 1e-12 for v, m in zip(vals, row)),
                    f"{[round(v, 3) for v in vals]}")
    print()
    print("  Also: the tropical binomial form agrees everywhere.")
    good = all(
        abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t) - kstar_tropical(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t)) < 1e-12
        for s in (0.0, 0.5, 1.44997, 2.0, 3.3) for t in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0)
    )
    ok &= check("k* = max(k0, k0 + delta*t - delta*sigma)", good)
    return ok


def demo_rigidity() -> bool:
    header("4. Continuous rigidity: two local laws determine the whole plane")
    print("  Build a table only from the base profile and the two laws, then")
    print("  check it agrees with the closed form k*(s, t) = k0 + d*(t-s)^+.")

    base = lambda x: affine_interp(K0_BASE, DELTA, x)

    def table_from_laws(sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
        # Transport (sigma, t) to the base row / base-context edge, exactly as
        # in the proof of the rigidity theorem.
        if t <= sigma:
            return base(0.0)          # base-context inertia
        return base(t - sigma)        # slide down the flow direction (1,1)

    ok = all(
        abs(table_from_laws(s, t) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t)) < 1e-12
        for s in (0.0, 0.37, 1.0, 1.44997, 2.0, 5.0)
        for t in (0.0, 0.37, 1.0, 2.0, 3.5, 7.0)
    )
    return check("rigidity reconstruction matches the closed form", ok)


def demo_lipschitz() -> bool:
    header("5. Lipschitz transport in scale: no cliffs between measured rows")
    worst = 0.0
    for t in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0):
        for s in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0):
            for h in (0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0):
                gap = abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s + h, t))
                worst = max(worst, gap - DELTA * h)
    return check("|k*(s,t) - k*(s+h,t)| <= delta*h everywhere sampled",
                 worst <= 1e-12, f"max excess = {worst:.3e}")


def demo_interpolation_nonuniqueness() -> bool:
    header("6. Monotone interpolation exists — but is NOT unique")
    ok = True
    print("  Both interpolants hit every measured cell:")
    good_pl = all(abs(pl_interp(base_chain, float(n)) - base_chain(n)) < 1e-12
                  for n in range(6))
    good_st = all(abs(ceil_interp(base_chain, float(n)) - base_chain(n)) < 1e-12
                  for n in range(6))
    ok &= check("ramp-basis interpolant passes through every cell", good_pl)
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant passes through every cell", good_st)

    print("  Both are monotone:")
    grid = [i / 20.0 for i in range(101)]
    mono_pl = all(pl_interp(base_chain, a) <= pl_interp(base_chain, b) + 1e-12
                  for a, b in zip(grid, grid[1:]))
    mono_st = all(ceil_interp(base_chain, a) <= ceil_interp(base_chain, b) + 1e-12
                  for a, b in zip(grid, grid[1:]))
    ok &= check("ramp-basis interpolant is monotone", mono_pl)
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant is monotone", mono_st)

    print("  Yet they disagree at the half-octave:")
    pl_half = pl_interp(base_chain, 0.5)
    st_half = ceil_interp(base_chain, 0.5)
    ok &= check("PL(1/2) = 18 and ST(1/2) = 20 — a four-key gap",
                abs(pl_half - 18.0) < 1e-12 and abs(st_half - 20.0) < 1e-12,
                f"PL = {pl_half}, ST = {st_half}, gap = {st_half - pl_half}")
    return ok


def demo_generator_theorem() -> bool:
    header("7. Stationary increments force affinity (generator theorem)")
    print("  The staircase interpolant is monotone and interpolating, but its")
    print("  increments are NOT stationary; the ramp interpolant of an")
    print("  arithmetic chain is affine and its increments ARE stationary.")

    def stationarity_defect(f: Callable[[float], float]) -> float:
        worst = 0.0
        for t in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.75, 2.5):
            for u in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.75):
                lhs = f(t + u) - f(t)
                rhs = f(u) - f(0.0)
                worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs))
        return worst

    d_pl = stationarity_defect(lambda x: pl_interp(base_chain, x))
    d_st = stationarity_defect(lambda x: ceil_interp(base_chain, x))
    ok = True
    ok &= check("ramp interpolant has stationary increments",
                d_pl < 1e-12, f"defect = {d_pl:.3e}")
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant does NOT",
                d_st > 0.5, f"defect = {d_st:.3f} keys")
    print()
    print("  Generator theorem: monotone + stationary  =>  K0(t) = K0(0) + delta*t")
    slope = pl_interp(base_chain, 1.0) - pl_interp(base_chain, 0.0)
    good = all(abs(pl_interp(base_chain, t)
                   - (pl_interp(base_chain, 0.0) + slope * t)) < 1e-12
               for t in [i / 8.0 for i in range(40)])
    ok &= check("the unique stationary monotone interpolant is 16 + 4t",
                good and abs(slope - DELTA) < 1e-12,
                f"delta = K0(1) - K0(0) = {slope}")
    return ok


def demo_transport_equation() -> bool:
    header("8. The generator is the keys-per-octave rate; transport equation")
    h = 1e-6
    ok = True
    for sigma, t in ((1.0, 2.0), (0.5, 3.0), (1.44997, 2.0)):
        d_sigma = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma + h, t)
                   - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma - h, t)) / (2 * h)
        d_t = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t + h)
               - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t - h)) / (2 * h)
        ok &= check(f"at (sigma, t) = ({sigma}, {t}):  d/dsigma = -delta, d/dt = +delta,"
                    f" sum = 0",
                    abs(d_sigma + DELTA) < 1e-5 and abs(d_t - DELTA) < 1e-5
                    and abs(d_sigma + d_t) < 1e-6,
                    f"({d_sigma:+.4f}, {d_t:+.4f}) -> {d_sigma + d_t:+.2e}")
    return ok


def demo_3B_sweep() -> bool:
    header("9. The 3B sweep: filling in the row nobody measured")
    s3 = scale_index(3.0)
    ok = True
    ok &= check("scaleIndex(1.5) = 1", abs(scale_index(1.5) - 1.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("scaleIndex(7) = 2", abs(scale_index(7.0) - 2.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("7/5 < scaleIndex(3) < 3/2  (strictly fractional offset)",
                1.4 < s3 < 1.5, f"scaleIndex(3) = {s3:.6f}")
    print()
    print("  Predicted knee chain (ctx tokens -> exact value -> deployable budget):")
    ctxs = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]
    for ctx in ctxs:
        t = math.log2(ctx / BASE_CTX)
        val = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, t)
        print(f"    ctx = {ctx:5d} : k* = {val:7.4f}  ->  budget {math.ceil(val):3d}")
    print()
    k2 = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 2.0)
    k3 = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 3.0)
    ok &= check("3B at 512 and 1024 is still flat at 16 keys",
                abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 0.0) - 16.0) < 1e-12
                and abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 1.0) - 16.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("18 < k*(3B, 2048) < 18.4  and  ceil = 19",
                18.0 < k2 < 18.4 and math.ceil(k2) == 19, f"k* = {k2:.6f}")
    ok &= check("22 < k*(3B, 4096) < 22.4  and  ceil = 23",
                22.0 < k3 < 22.4 and math.ceil(k3) == 23, f"k* = {k3:.6f}")
    ok &= check("bracketed strictly by the 7B and 1.5B cells at 2048",
                kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 2.0, 2.0) < k2 < kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.0, 2.0),
                f"16 < {k2:.4f} < 20")
    ok &= check("no integer scale index reproduces it (falsifiable prediction)",
                all(abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, float(s), 2.0) - k2) > 1e-6
                    for s in range(0, 12)))
    print()
    print("  Full interpolated deployment table:")
    print(f"    {'model':>8} | " + " | ".join(f"{c:>5}" for c in ctxs))
    print("    " + "-" * (10 + 8 * len(ctxs)))
    for n in (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0, 13.0):
        row = " | ".join(f"{deployable_budget(n, c):5d}" for c in ctxs)
        print(f"    {n:6.1f}B | {row}")
    print()
    print("  NOTE.  The calibration is anchored on the two CONSECUTIVE rows")
    print("  1.5B -> 1 and 7B -> 2.  The measured ladder is not geometric")
    print("  (1.5/0.5 = 3 but 7/1.5 = 14/3), so the third row is over-determined:")
    print(f"  this calibration places 0.5B at sigma = {scale_index(0.5):.4f}, not 0, and")
    print("  its interpolated row (16, 19, 23, 27) undershoots the measured")
    print("  (16, 20, 24, 28) by one key.  The knee table itself is exact at every")
    print("  integer scale index; the residual is in the size-to-index calibration,")
    print("  and it is precisely the kind of deviation a third anchor can test.")
    return ok


def demo_identifiability() -> bool:
    header("10. The rate is data, not a fitting convention")
    print("  If two clamped-affine tables agree at every real context, their")
    print("  base knee, rate and offset must all agree.  Perturb any one of")
    print("  them and the tables separate:")
    ok = True
    ref = lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.0, t)
    grid = [i / 4.0 for i in range(0, 25)]
    for label, f in (
        ("perturbed rate    (delta 4 -> 4.5)", lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, 4.5, 1.0, t)),
        ("perturbed base    (k0 16 -> 16.5)", lambda t: kstar(16.5, DELTA, 1.0, t)),
        ("perturbed offset  (sigma 1 -> 1.1)", lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.1, t)),
    ):
        sep = max(abs(ref(t) - f(t)) for t in grid)
        ok &= check(f"{label} separates the tables", sep > 1e-9,
                    f"max |diff| = {sep:.4f} keys")
    print()
    print("  And the measured cells force (k0, delta) = (16, 4):")
    k0_forced = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 0.0, 0.0)                       # clamp active
    delta_forced = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 0.0, 1.0) - k0_forced        # clamp inactive
    ok &= check("k0 = 16 and delta = 4 are forced by the 0.5B row",
                abs(k0_forced - 16.0) < 1e-12 and abs(delta_forced - 4.0) < 1e-12,
                f"(k0, delta) = ({k0_forced}, {delta_forced})")
    return ok


def demo_reach_and_defect() -> bool:
    header("11. Budget reach, the served region, and the exact S/2 defect")
    ok = True
    print("  Budget adjunction:  k*(sigma, t) <= b   <=>   t <= sigma + reach(b).")
    for b in (16.0, 20.0, 24.0, 28.0):
        r = reach(K0_BASE, DELTA, b)
        good = True
        for sigma in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.44997, 2.0, 3.0):
            for t in [i / 4.0 for i in range(0, 33)]:
                lhs = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t) <= b + 1e-12
                rhs = t <= sigma + r + 1e-12
                good &= (lhs == rhs)
        ok &= check(f"budget b = {b:.0f} keys has reach {r:.1f} octaves; adjunction holds",
                    good)
    print()
    print("  Continuous budget law: the served boundary is a line of slope 1.")
    r16 = reach(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0)
    ok &= check("a 16-key budget has reach 0 (boundary is the diagonal t = sigma)",
                abs(r16) < 1e-12)
    print()
    print("  Staircase (discrete cells) vs triangle (continuous area):")
    print(f"    {'S':>3} | {'cells':>7} | {'area':>8} | {'defect':>8} | {'S/2':>6}")
    print("    " + "-" * 44)
    for S in range(0, 9):
        J = max(S, 1) + 4
        cells = served_cells(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0, S, J)
        area = served_area(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0, float(S))
        defect = cells - area
        print(f"    {S:3d} | {cells:7d} | {area:8.2f} | {defect:8.2f} | {S / 2:6.2f}")
        ok &= abs(defect - S / 2.0) < 1e-12
    ok = check("discrete served cells - continuous served area = S/2, exactly", ok)
    return ok


def demo_tropical_corner() -> bool:
    header("12. The tropical corner: one knee per model, on the diagonal")
    ok = True
    sigma = 1.44997
    h = 1e-7

    def one_sided(t: float, side: int) -> float:
        if side > 0:
            return (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t + h)
                    - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t)) / h
        return (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t)
                - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t - h)) / h

    left = one_sided(sigma, -1)
    right = one_sided(sigma, +1)
    ok &= check("at t = sigma the one-sided slopes are 0 (left) and delta (right)",
                abs(left) < 1e-5 and abs(right - DELTA) < 1e-5,
                f"left = {left:.6f}, right = {right:.6f}")
    print("  Away from the diagonal the two one-sided slopes agree (smooth):")
    for t in (sigma - 0.6, sigma + 0.6, sigma + 2.0):
        l, r = one_sided(t, -1), one_sided(t, +1)
        ok &= check(f"t = {t:.4f} is a smooth point", abs(l - r) < 1e-5,
                    f"slopes {l:.4f} / {r:.4f}")
    print()
    print("  Corner locus is invariant under the flow direction (1, 1):")
    good = True
    for a in (0.0, 0.5, 1.3, 2.7):
        # corner of the shifted table sits at sigma + a
        s2 = sigma + a
        lf = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s2, s2) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s2, s2 - h)) / h
        rt = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s2, s2 + h) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s2, s2)) / h
        good &= abs(lf) < 1e-5 and abs(rt - DELTA) < 1e-5
    ok &= check("shifting scale by a shifts the corner by a", good)
    print()
    print("  Convexity (diminishing returns) along both axes:")
    def convex_on(f: Callable[[float], float], xs: Sequence[float]) -> bool:
        return all(f((a + c) / 2) <= (f(a) + f(c)) / 2 + 1e-12
                   for a in xs for c in xs)
    xs = [i / 4.0 for i in range(-8, 25)]
    ok &= check("convex in context",
                convex_on(lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.0, t), xs))
    ok &= check("convex in scale",
                convex_on(lambda s: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, 3.0), xs))
    return ok

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Measured data (the reference family)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

BASE_CTX: int = 512                 # context length of octave 0
K0_BASE: float = 16.0               # base knee, in keys
DELTA: float = 4.0                  # keys per octave

# Measured knee table: rows are scale indices 0, 1, 2 (0.5B, 1.5B, 7B),
# columns are context octaves 0..3 (512, 1024, 2048, 4096 tokens).
MEASURED_TABLE: Dict[int, List[int]] = {
    0: [16, 20, 24, 28],
    1: [16, 16, 20, 24],
    2: [16, 16, 16, 20],
}

MODEL_ANCHORS: Dict[float, int] = {1.5: 1, 7.0: 2}   # billions of params -> index


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Ordered subtraction, in both monoids
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def nat_tsub(j: int, s: int) -> int:
    """Truncated subtraction in (N, +): j - s clamped at 0."""
    return j - s if j >= s else 0


def real_tsub(t: float, s: float) -> float:
    """Ordered subtraction in (R>=0, +): exactly the clamp max(t - s, 0)."""
    return max(t - s, 0.0)


def base_chain(j: int) -> int:
    """The measured base chain K(j) = 16 + 4j (the 0.5B row)."""
    return 16 + 4 * j


def shift(chain: Callable[[int], int], s: int) -> Callable[[int], int]:
    """The discrete octave shift: (shift K s)(j) = K(j - s), truncated."""
    return lambda j: chain(nat_tsub(j, s))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The canonical real table
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kstar(k0: float, delta: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
    """k*(sigma, t) = k0 + delta * (t - sigma)^+  — the canonical real table."""
    return k0 + delta * real_tsub(t, sigma)


def kstar_tropical(k0: float, delta: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
    """Tropical binomial form: max-plus sum of monomials k0 and k0 + d t - d s."""
    return max(k0, k0 + delta * t - delta * sigma)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Interpolants of a measured chain
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ramp(x: float) -> float:
    """Unit ramp: 0 below 0, linear on [0, 1], 1 above 1."""
    return min(1.0, max(x, 0.0))


def pl_interp(chain: Callable[[int], int], t: float) -> float:
    """Ramp-basis (piecewise-linear) interpolant of a measured chain.

    PL_K(t) = K(0) + sum_{i < ceil(t)} (K(i+1) - K(i)) * ramp(t - i).
    Monotone whenever K is, because every coefficient is nonnegative and every
    basis function is monotone.
    """
    total = float(chain(0))
    for i in range(math.ceil(t)):
        total += (chain(i + 1) - chain(i)) * ramp(t - i)
    return total


def ceil_interp(chain: Callable[[int], int], t: float) -> float:
    """Staircase interpolant: round the context octave up to the next measured one."""
    return float(chain(math.ceil(t)))


def affine_interp(k0: float, delta: float, t: float) -> float:
    """The affine profile k0 + delta * t (unique monotone stationary interpolant)."""
    return k0 + delta * t


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Scale-axis calibration
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def scale_index(n_billion: float) -> float:
    """Log-linear scale index, anchored at 1.5B -> 1 and 7B -> 2."""
    return 1.0 + math.log(n_billion / 1.5) / math.log(14.0 / 3.0)


def deployable_budget(n_billion: float, ctx_tokens: int,
                      k0: float = K0_BASE, delta: float = DELTA) -> int:
    """Interpolated, deployable (integer) key budget for any model size / context."""
    sigma = scale_index(n_billion)
    t = math.log2(ctx_tokens / BASE_CTX)
    return math.ceil(kstar(k0, delta, sigma, t))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Budget reach and served region
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def reach(k0: float, delta: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Reach of a budget: the number of context octaves above base it buys."""
    return (b - k0) / delta


def served_cells(k0: float, delta: float, b: float, S: int, J: int) -> int:
    """Number of served cells of the DISCRETE table over scale rows 0..S-1."""
    count = 0
    for s in range(S):
        for j in range(J + 1):
            if kstar(k0, delta, float(s), float(j)) <= b + 1e-12:
                count += 1
    return count


def served_area(k0: float, delta: float, b: float, S: float) -> float:
    """Area under the CONTINUOUS served boundary t = sigma + reach over [0, S]."""
    r = reach(k0, delta, b)
    # integral_0^S (sigma + r) dsigma  =  S^2/2 + r*S ; with r = 0 this is S^2/2.
    return S * S / 2.0 + r * S


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def header(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def check(label: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> bool:
    mark = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    line = f"  [{mark}] {label}"
    if detail:
        line += f"   {detail}"
    print(line)
    return ok


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_octave_shift_law() -> bool:
    header("1. The discrete octave shift law: one chain, translated")
    print("  Measured table (rows = scale index, cols = context octave 0..3):")
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        print(f"    sigma = {s} : {row}")
    print()
    print("  Claim: every cell equals K(j - s) with K(j) = 16 + 4j, truncated.")
    ok = True
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        shifted = [shift(base_chain, s)(j) for j in range(len(row))]
        ok &= check(f"row sigma = {s} is the base chain shifted by {s}",
                    shifted == row, f"{shifted}")
    return ok


def demo_monoid_action() -> bool:
    header("2. The shift extends to an action of (R>=0, +)")
    print("  rho_s K(t) = K(max(t - s, 0)).  Check rho_0 = id and")
    print("  rho_b o rho_a = rho_{a+b} at many random-ish sample points.")
    profile = lambda x: affine_interp(K0_BASE, DELTA, x)
    ok = True
    samples = [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.3333, 2.0, 2.7, 3.5, 5.0]
    ok &= check("rho_0 is the identity",
                all(abs(profile(real_tsub(t, 0.0)) - profile(t)) < 1e-12
                    for t in samples))
    pairs = [(0.3, 0.7), (1.0, 1.0), (0.45, 2.2), (1.44997, 0.55003)]
    good = True
    for a, b in pairs:
        for t in samples:
            lhs = profile(real_tsub(real_tsub(t, a), b))
            rhs = profile(real_tsub(t, a + b))
            good &= abs(lhs - rhs) < 1e-12
    ok &= check("rho_b o rho_a = rho_{a+b} (associativity of the action)", good)

    # exchange law
    good = all(
        abs(profile(real_tsub(t + a, s + a)) - profile(real_tsub(t, s))) < 1e-12
        for s in samples for t in samples for a in (0.0, 0.5, 1.7)
    )
    ok &= check("exchange law: a octaves of scale buy a octaves of context", good)
    return ok


def demo_restriction() -> bool:
    header("3. The real flow restricts to the measured cells")
    ok = True
    for s, row in MEASURED_TABLE.items():
        vals = [kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, float(s), float(j)) for j in range(len(row))]
        ok &= check(f"k*({s}, j) reproduces the sigma = {s} row",
                    all(abs(v - m) < 1e-12 for v, m in zip(vals, row)),
                    f"{[round(v, 3) for v in vals]}")
    print()
    print("  Also: the tropical binomial form agrees everywhere.")
    good = all(
        abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t) - kstar_tropical(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t)) < 1e-12
        for s in (0.0, 0.5, 1.44997, 2.0, 3.3) for t in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0)
    )
    ok &= check("k* = max(k0, k0 + delta*t - delta*sigma)", good)
    return ok


def demo_rigidity() -> bool:
    header("4. Continuous rigidity: two local laws determine the whole plane")
    print("  Build a table only from the base profile and the two laws, then")
    print("  check it agrees with the closed form k*(s, t) = k0 + d*(t-s)^+.")

    base = lambda x: affine_interp(K0_BASE, DELTA, x)

    def table_from_laws(sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
        # Transport (sigma, t) to the base row / base-context edge, exactly as
        # in the proof of the rigidity theorem.
        if t <= sigma:
            return base(0.0)          # base-context inertia
        return base(t - sigma)        # slide down the flow direction (1,1)

    ok = all(
        abs(table_from_laws(s, t) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t)) < 1e-12
        for s in (0.0, 0.37, 1.0, 1.44997, 2.0, 5.0)
        for t in (0.0, 0.37, 1.0, 2.0, 3.5, 7.0)
    )
    return check("rigidity reconstruction matches the closed form", ok)


def demo_lipschitz() -> bool:
    header("5. Lipschitz transport in scale: no cliffs between measured rows")
    worst = 0.0
    for t in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0):
        for s in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0):
            for h in (0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0):
                gap = abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s, t) - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s + h, t))
                worst = max(worst, gap - DELTA * h)
    return check("|k*(s,t) - k*(s+h,t)| <= delta*h everywhere sampled",
                 worst <= 1e-12, f"max excess = {worst:.3e}")


def demo_interpolation_nonuniqueness() -> bool:
    header("6. Monotone interpolation exists — but is NOT unique")
    ok = True
    print("  Both interpolants hit every measured cell:")
    good_pl = all(abs(pl_interp(base_chain, float(n)) - base_chain(n)) < 1e-12
                  for n in range(6))
    good_st = all(abs(ceil_interp(base_chain, float(n)) - base_chain(n)) < 1e-12
                  for n in range(6))
    ok &= check("ramp-basis interpolant passes through every cell", good_pl)
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant passes through every cell", good_st)

    print("  Both are monotone:")
    grid = [i / 20.0 for i in range(101)]
    mono_pl = all(pl_interp(base_chain, a) <= pl_interp(base_chain, b) + 1e-12
                  for a, b in zip(grid, grid[1:]))
    mono_st = all(ceil_interp(base_chain, a) <= ceil_interp(base_chain, b) + 1e-12
                  for a, b in zip(grid, grid[1:]))
    ok &= check("ramp-basis interpolant is monotone", mono_pl)
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant is monotone", mono_st)

    print("  Yet they disagree at the half-octave:")
    pl_half = pl_interp(base_chain, 0.5)
    st_half = ceil_interp(base_chain, 0.5)
    ok &= check("PL(1/2) = 18 and ST(1/2) = 20 — a four-key gap",
                abs(pl_half - 18.0) < 1e-12 and abs(st_half - 20.0) < 1e-12,
                f"PL = {pl_half}, ST = {st_half}, gap = {st_half - pl_half}")
    return ok


def demo_generator_theorem() -> bool:
    header("7. Stationary increments force affinity (generator theorem)")
    print("  The staircase interpolant is monotone and interpolating, but its")
    print("  increments are NOT stationary; the ramp interpolant of an")
    print("  arithmetic chain is affine and its increments ARE stationary.")

    def stationarity_defect(f: Callable[[float], float]) -> float:
        worst = 0.0
        for t in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.75, 2.5):
            for u in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.75):
                lhs = f(t + u) - f(t)
                rhs = f(u) - f(0.0)
                worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs))
        return worst

    d_pl = stationarity_defect(lambda x: pl_interp(base_chain, x))
    d_st = stationarity_defect(lambda x: ceil_interp(base_chain, x))
    ok = True
    ok &= check("ramp interpolant has stationary increments",
                d_pl < 1e-12, f"defect = {d_pl:.3e}")
    ok &= check("staircase interpolant does NOT",
                d_st > 0.5, f"defect = {d_st:.3f} keys")
    print()
    print("  Generator theorem: monotone + stationary  =>  K0(t) = K0(0) + delta*t")
    slope = pl_interp(base_chain, 1.0) - pl_interp(base_chain, 0.0)
    good = all(abs(pl_interp(base_chain, t)
                   - (pl_interp(base_chain, 0.0) + slope * t)) < 1e-12
               for t in [i / 8.0 for i in range(40)])
    ok &= check("the unique stationary monotone interpolant is 16 + 4t",
                good and abs(slope - DELTA) < 1e-12,
                f"delta = K0(1) - K0(0) = {slope}")
    return ok


def demo_transport_equation() -> bool:
    header("8. The generator is the keys-per-octave rate; transport equation")
    h = 1e-6
    ok = True
    for sigma, t in ((1.0, 2.0), (0.5, 3.0), (1.44997, 2.0)):
        d_sigma = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma + h, t)
                   - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma - h, t)) / (2 * h)
        d_t = (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t + h)
               - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t - h)) / (2 * h)
        ok &= check(f"at (sigma, t) = ({sigma}, {t}):  d/dsigma = -delta, d/dt = +delta,"
                    f" sum = 0",
                    abs(d_sigma + DELTA) < 1e-5 and abs(d_t - DELTA) < 1e-5
                    and abs(d_sigma + d_t) < 1e-6,
                    f"({d_sigma:+.4f}, {d_t:+.4f}) -> {d_sigma + d_t:+.2e}")
    return ok


def demo_3B_sweep() -> bool:
    header("9. The 3B sweep: filling in the row nobody measured")
    s3 = scale_index(3.0)
    ok = True
    ok &= check("scaleIndex(1.5) = 1", abs(scale_index(1.5) - 1.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("scaleIndex(7) = 2", abs(scale_index(7.0) - 2.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("7/5 < scaleIndex(3) < 3/2  (strictly fractional offset)",
                1.4 < s3 < 1.5, f"scaleIndex(3) = {s3:.6f}")
    print()
    print("  Predicted knee chain (ctx tokens -> exact value -> deployable budget):")
    ctxs = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]
    for ctx in ctxs:
        t = math.log2(ctx / BASE_CTX)
        val = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, t)
        print(f"    ctx = {ctx:5d} : k* = {val:7.4f}  ->  budget {math.ceil(val):3d}")
    print()
    k2 = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 2.0)
    k3 = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 3.0)
    ok &= check("3B at 512 and 1024 is still flat at 16 keys",
                abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 0.0) - 16.0) < 1e-12
                and abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, s3, 1.0) - 16.0) < 1e-12)
    ok &= check("18 < k*(3B, 2048) < 18.4  and  ceil = 19",
                18.0 < k2 < 18.4 and math.ceil(k2) == 19, f"k* = {k2:.6f}")
    ok &= check("22 < k*(3B, 4096) < 22.4  and  ceil = 23",
                22.0 < k3 < 22.4 and math.ceil(k3) == 23, f"k* = {k3:.6f}")
    ok &= check("bracketed strictly by the 7B and 1.5B cells at 2048",
                kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 2.0, 2.0) < k2 < kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.0, 2.0),
                f"16 < {k2:.4f} < 20")
    ok &= check("no integer scale index reproduces it (falsifiable prediction)",
                all(abs(kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, float(s), 2.0) - k2) > 1e-6
                    for s in range(0, 12)))
    print()
    print("  Full interpolated deployment table:")
    print(f"    {'model':>8} | " + " | ".join(f"{c:>5}" for c in ctxs))
    print("    " + "-" * (10 + 8 * len(ctxs)))
    for n in (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0, 13.0):
        row = " | ".join(f"{deployable_budget(n, c):5d}" for c in ctxs)
        print(f"    {n:6.1f}B | {row}")
    print()
    print("  NOTE.  The calibration is anchored on the two CONSECUTIVE rows")
    print("  1.5B -> 1 and 7B -> 2.  The measured ladder is not geometric")
    print("  (1.5/0.5 = 3 but 7/1.5 = 14/3), so the third row is over-determined:")
    print(f"  this calibration places 0.5B at sigma = {scale_index(0.5):.4f}, not 0, and")
    print("  its interpolated row (16, 19, 23, 27) undershoots the measured")
    print("  (16, 20, 24, 28) by one key.  The knee table itself is exact at every")
    print("  integer scale index; the residual is in the size-to-index calibration,")
    print("  and it is precisely the kind of deviation a third anchor can test.")
    return ok


def demo_identifiability() -> bool:
    header("10. The rate is data, not a fitting convention")
    print("  If two clamped-affine tables agree at every real context, their")
    print("  base knee, rate and offset must all agree.  Perturb any one of")
    print("  them and the tables separate:")
    ok = True
    ref = lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.0, t)
    grid = [i / 4.0 for i in range(0, 25)]
    for label, f in (
        ("perturbed rate    (delta 4 -> 4.5)", lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, 4.5, 1.0, t)),
        ("perturbed base    (k0 16 -> 16.5)", lambda t: kstar(16.5, DELTA, 1.0, t)),
        ("perturbed offset  (sigma 1 -> 1.1)", lambda t: kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 1.1, t)),
    ):
        sep = max(abs(ref(t) - f(t)) for t in grid)
        ok &= check(f"{label} separates the tables", sep > 1e-9,
                    f"max |diff| = {sep:.4f} keys")
    print()
    print("  And the measured cells force (k0, delta) = (16, 4):")
    k0_forced = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 0.0, 0.0)                       # clamp active
    delta_forced = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, 0.0, 1.0) - k0_forced        # clamp inactive
    ok &= check("k0 = 16 and delta = 4 are forced by the 0.5B row",
                abs(k0_forced - 16.0) < 1e-12 and abs(delta_forced - 4.0) < 1e-12,
                f"(k0, delta) = ({k0_forced}, {delta_forced})")
    return ok


def demo_reach_and_defect() -> bool:
    header("11. Budget reach, the served region, and the exact S/2 defect")
    ok = True
    print("  Budget adjunction:  k*(sigma, t) <= b   <=>   t <= sigma + reach(b).")
    for b in (16.0, 20.0, 24.0, 28.0):
        r = reach(K0_BASE, DELTA, b)
        good = True
        for sigma in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.44997, 2.0, 3.0):
            for t in [i / 4.0 for i in range(0, 33)]:
                lhs = kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t) <= b + 1e-12
                rhs = t <= sigma + r + 1e-12
                good &= (lhs == rhs)
        ok &= check(f"budget b = {b:.0f} keys has reach {r:.1f} octaves; adjunction holds",
                    good)
    print()
    print("  Continuous budget law: the served boundary is a line of slope 1.")
    r16 = reach(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0)
    ok &= check("a 16-key budget has reach 0 (boundary is the diagonal t = sigma)",
                abs(r16) < 1e-12)
    print()
    print("  Staircase (discrete cells) vs triangle (continuous area):")
    print(f"    {'S':>3} | {'cells':>7} | {'area':>8} | {'defect':>8} | {'S/2':>6}")
    print("    " + "-" * 44)
    for S in range(0, 9):
        J = max(S, 1) + 4
        cells = served_cells(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0, S, J)
        area = served_area(K0_BASE, DELTA, 16.0, float(S))
        defect = cells - area
        print(f"    {S:3d} | {cells:7d} | {area:8.2f} | {defect:8.2f} | {S / 2:6.2f}")
        ok &= abs(defect - S / 2.0) < 1e-12
    ok = check("discrete served cells - continuous served area = S/2, exactly", ok)
    return ok


def demo_tropical_corner() -> bool:
    header("12. The tropical corner: one knee per model, on the diagonal")
    ok = True
    sigma = 1.44997
    h = 1e-7

    def one_sided(t: float, side: int) -> float:
        if side > 0:
            return (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t + h)
                    - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t)) / h
        return (kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t)
                - kstar(K0_BASE, DELTA, sigma, t - h)) / h

    left = one_sided(sigma, -1)
    right = one_sided(sigma, +1)
    ok &= check("at t = sigma the one-sided slopes are 0 (left) and delta (right)",
                abs(left) < 1e-5 and abs(right - DELTA) < 1e-5,
                f"left = {left:.6f}, right = {right:.6f}")
    print("  Away from the diagonal the two one-sided slopes agree (smooth):")

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple


def nat_tsub(j: int, s: int) -> int:
    """Truncated subtraction in (N, +): j - s clamped at zero."""
    return j - s if j >= s else 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChainFit:
    """Outcome of fitting an octave-shift law to a measured knee table."""
    base_chain: Tuple[int, ...]
    obeys_shift_law: bool
    violations: Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int, int], ...]   # (s, j, observed, predicted)

def _ramp(x: float) -> float:
    """Unit ramp: 0 below 0, linear on [0, 1], 1 above 1."""
    return min(1.0, max(x, 0.0))


def _ramp_profile(chain: Sequence[int]) -> Callable[[float], float]:
    """Ramp-basis interpolant of a measured chain, as a callable on [0, inf)."""
    def profile(t: float) -> float:
        total = float(chain[0])
        for i in range(min(math.ceil(t - 1e-12), len(chain) - 1)):
            total += (chain[i + 1] - chain[i]) * _ramp(t - i)
        return total
    return profile


def _affine_profile(k0: float, delta: float) -> Callable[[float], float]:
    """The affine profile k0 + delta * t."""
    return lambda t: k0 + delta * t

    if 0 not in table:

    base: Tuple[int, ...] = tuple(table[0])

    violations: List[Tuple[int, int, int, int]] = []
    for s, row in sorted(table.items()):

            idx = nat_tsub(j, s)
            if idx >= len(base):

            predicted = base[idx]
            if observed != predicted:

        delta: Optional[float] = float(diffs[0])

        obeys_shift_law=not violations,
        violations=tuple(violations),
        monotone=monotone,
        arithmetic=arithmetic,
        k0=k0,

        profile=profile,

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Calibration:
    """Two-anchor log-linear calibration of the scale axis."""
    n_small: float          # model size (billions) at the smaller anchor
    sigma_small: float      # its scale index
    n_large: float          # model size (billions) at the larger anchor
    sigma_large: float      # its scale index

    def scale_index(self, n_billion: float) -> float:
        """sigma(N): strictly increasing, hitting both anchors exactly."""
        if n_billion <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError("model size must be positive")
        span_sigma = self.sigma_large - self.sigma_small
        span_log = math.log(self.n_large / self.n_small)
        return self.sigma_small + span_sigma * math.log(n_billion / self.n_small) / span_log


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BudgetQuery:
    """Result of an interpolated budget query."""
    model_billion: float
    ctx_tokens: int
    scale_index: float
    context_octave: float
    knee_exact: float
    knee_budget: int
    lower_neighbour: Tuple[int, float]     # (integer scale index, its knee)
    upper_neighbour: Tuple[int, float]
    is_discrete_cell: bool                 # reachable by some integer scale index?


def kstar(k0: float, delta: float, sigma: float, t: float) -> float:
    """k*(sigma, t) = k0 + delta * max(t - sigma, 0)."""
    return k0 + delta * max(t - sigma, 0.0)


def interpolated_budget(model_billion: float,
                        ctx_tokens: int,
                        k0: float,
                        delta: float,
                        calib: Calibration,
                        base_ctx: int = 512,
                        max_scale: int = 16) -> BudgetQuery:
